---
title: "Primary Analysis: LCM-SR"
author: "XXXX"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output: html_document
---

This file runs the primary analysis: missing data checks, descriptive statistics, the model-building steps for the latent curve model with structured residuals (LCM-SR), and the final model. The models are estimated in Mplus (version 9) through the MplusAutomation package, and all Mplus input and output files are saved in the working folder. The sensitivity analysis scripts (2 to 5) compare their results with the final model from this file, so run this file first.

Results that feed a table or section of the manuscript are labelled, and key results are saved as CSV files for checking.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)

library(dplyr)
library(MplusAutomation)
library(naniar)
library(logistf)
library(psych)
library(diptest)

# Set WD
set.seed(123)
setwd("C:XXXX")

# Import data
GZMCore <- readRDS("C:XXXX")

# Fit indices reported in the tables
fit_cols <- c("Title", "Parameters", "ChiSqM_Value", "ChiSqM_DF", "ChiSqM_PValue",
              "CFI", "RMSEA_Estimate", "RMSEA_90CI_LB", "RMSEA_90CI_UB", "SRMR", "AIC", "BIC")

# Scaled chi-square difference test for models estimated with MLR
# (Satorra-Bentler, calculated from the log-likelihoods)
# "simpler" is the model with fewer parameters, "fuller" the model with more
scaled_diff_test <- function(simpler, fuller) {
  m0 <- readModels(simpler, what = "summaries")$summaries
  m1 <- readModels(fuller,  what = "summaries")$summaries
  df_diff    <- m1$Parameters - m0$Parameters
  scaling    <- (m1$Parameters * m1$LLCorrectionFactor - m0$Parameters * m0$LLCorrectionFactor) / df_diff
  chisq_diff <- -2 * (m0$LL - m1$LL) / scaling
  c(ChiSq_diff = round(chisq_diff, 3),
    df         = df_diff,
    p          = round(pchisq(chisq_diff, df_diff, lower.tail = FALSE), 4))
}
```

# Part 1: Missing Data (Supplementary Material S1)

```{r missing completely at random}
# Little's test of whether data are missing completely at random
GZMCore %>%
  select(StressComp_W0, StressComp_W1, StressComp_W2, StressComp_W3, StressComp_W4,
         DASS_Total_W0, DASS_Total_W1, DASS_Total_W2, DASS_Total_W3, DASS_Total_W4,
         m_W1, m_W2, m_W3, m_W4) %>%
  mcar_test()
```

```{r retention}
# Which baseline characteristics predict still taking part at W4?
# Firth logistic regression is used because it handles small or uneven groups well
retention <- GZMCore %>%
  transmute(
    # Retained = any score recorded at W4
    Retained = as.integer(!is.na(StressComp_W4) | !is.na(DASS_Total_W4) | !is.na(IntHom_W4) |
                          !is.na(NOSC_S_W4) | !is.na(SMARSS_W4) | !is.na(EISS_A_W4) | !is.na(m_W4)),
    Age,
    GenderDiverse = case_when(GenderGroup %in% c(1, 2) ~ 0, !is.na(GenderGroup) ~ 1),
    POC           = case_when(RaceAnalysis == 1 ~ 0, !is.na(RaceAnalysis) ~ 1),
    StressComp    = StressComp_W0,
    DASS_Total    = DASS_Total_W0,
    msbase
  )

cat("Retained at W4:", sum(retention$Retained), "of", nrow(retention), "\n")

retention_model <- logistf(Retained ~ Age + GenderDiverse + POC + StressComp + DASS_Total + msbase,
                           data = retention, control = logistf.control(maxit = 500))
summary(retention_model)
```

# Part 2: Descriptive Statistics

## Table 2

```{r table 2}
table2_vars <- c("StressComp_W0", "StressComp_W1", "StressComp_W2", "StressComp_W3", "StressComp_W4",
                 "DASS_Total_W0", "DASS_Total_W1", "DASS_Total_W2", "DASS_Total_W3", "DASS_Total_W4",
                 "m_W1", "m_W2", "m_W3", "m_W4")

# n, mean, SD and range
round(describe(GZMCore[, table2_vars])[, c("n", "mean", "sd", "min", "max")], 2)

# Pairwise correlations with Bonferroni correction
table2_cor <- corr.test(GZMCore[, table2_vars], use = "pairwise", adjust = "bonferroni")

# In the p-value file, Bonferroni-adjusted p-values are ABOVE the diagonal
# and unadjusted p-values are below it
write.csv(round(table2_cor$r, 2), "Table2_correlations.csv")
write.csv(signif(table2_cor$p, 3), "Table2_p_values.csv")
```

## Table 3

Baseline: mean age at each first experience and the percentage of the full sample who had it by baseline. Follow-ups: the percentage of participants who took part that wave and reported the experience in the past month.

```{r table 3}
experience_labels <- c("Attraction", "Self-identification", "Disclosure to family",
                       "Disclosure to someone else", "Non-heterosexual sexual activity",
                       "Non-heterosexual romantic relationship", "Heterosexual sexual activity",
                       "Heterosexual romantic relationship")

table_3 <- data.frame(
  Experience = experience_labels,
  W0_Age_M   = round(colMeans(GZMCore[, paste0("PSIM", 1:8)], na.rm = TRUE), 2),
  W0_Age_SD  = round(apply(GZMCore[, paste0("PSIM", 1:8)], 2, sd, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
  W0_pct     = round(100 * colSums(GZMCore[, paste0("USIM", 1:8, "_W0")] == 1, na.rm = TRUE) / nrow(GZMCore), 1),
  row.names  = NULL
)

for (w in 1:4) {
  # Participants with any score recorded that wave
  wave_scores <- GZMCore[, paste0(c("IntHom", "NOSC_S", "SMARSS", "StressComp", "StressComp_s",
                                    "EISS_A", "DASS_Total", "m", "m_w", "m_r"), "_W", w)]
  n_wave <- sum(rowSums(!is.na(wave_scores)) > 0)
  cat("W", w, "participants:", n_wave, "\n")

  experienced <- colSums(GZMCore[, paste0("USIM", 1:8, "_W", w)] == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  table_3[[paste0("W", w, "_pct")]] <- round(100 * experienced / n_wave, 1)
}

table_3
write.csv(table_3, "Table3_identity_experiences.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

# Part 3: Univariate Growth Models (Table S5)

## Mplus Data

Mplus uses short variable names: `x` = proximal minority stress composite, `y` = distress, and `m2` to `m5` = monthly identity development experience counts (W1 to W4). Missing values are coded -99.

```{r mplus data a}
GZMCore <- GZMCore %>%
  mutate(
    # Proximal minority stress composite (x) and distress (y), W0 to W4
    x1 = StressComp_W0, x2 = StressComp_W1, x3 = StressComp_W2, x4 = StressComp_W3, x5 = StressComp_W4,
    y1 = DASS_Total_W0, y2 = DASS_Total_W1, y3 = DASS_Total_W2, y4 = DASS_Total_W3, y5 = DASS_Total_W4,

    # Gender: 0 = cisgender, 1 = trans or gender diverse
    gender = case_when(GenderGroup %in% c(1, 2) ~ 0, GenderGroup %in% c(3, 4, 5, 6) ~ 1),

    # Ethnoracial identity: 0 = White, 1 = People of Colour
    race = case_when(RaceAnalysis == 1 ~ 0, RaceAnalysis == 2 ~ 1),

    # Age and baseline (lifetime) identity experience count, centred on the sample mean
    Age0    = Age - mean(Age, na.rm = TRUE),
    msbase0 = msbase - mean(msbase, na.rm = TRUE),

    # Baseline distress group: 0 = at or below the median, 1 = above the median
    dgrp = case_when(y1 <= median(y1, na.rm = TRUE) ~ 0, y1 > median(y1, na.rm = TRUE) ~ 1)
  )

mplus_a <- GZMCore %>%
  select(m_W1, m_W2, m_W3, m_W4, x1, x2, x3, x4, x5, y1, y2, y3, y4, y5,
         msbase0, Age0, gender, race)
mplus_a[is.na(mplus_a)] <- -99
prepareMplusData(mplus_a, "modela.dat")
```

## Growth Shape

Four trajectory shapes are compared for each construct: intercept only (no change), fixed linear slope (the same change for everyone), random linear slope (change differs between people) and freed time scores (non-linear change).

```{r univariate stress models}
# G1S: intercept only
mplusSyntaxG1S <- ("
TITLE: G1S Intercept-only growth model - Stress;

DATA:
  FILE = modela.dat;

VARIABLE:
  NAMES = m2-m5 x1-x5 y1-y5 msbase0 Age0 gender race;
  USEVARIABLES = x1-x5;
  MISSING = ALL(-99);

ANALYSIS:
  ESTIMATOR = MLR;
  PROCESSORS = 6;

MODEL:
  ! Intercept only — no slope
  ix | x1@0 x2@0 x3@0 x4@0 x5@0;
  [ix];
  ix;
  [x1-x5@0];

OUTPUT:
  TECH1 STDYX CINTERVAL;
")
writeLines(mplusSyntaxG1S, "modelg1s.inp")

# G2S: fixed linear slope
mplusSyntaxG2S <- ("
TITLE: G2S Fixed linear slope growth model - Stress;

DATA:
  FILE = modela.dat;

VARIABLE:
  NAMES = m2-m5 x1-x5 y1-y5 msbase0 Age0 gender race;
  USEVARIABLES = x1-x5;
  MISSING = ALL(-99);

ANALYSIS:
  ESTIMATOR = MLR;
  PROCESSORS = 6;

MODEL:
  ! Linear growth with fixed slope (no individual differences in trajectory)
  ix sx | x1@0 x2@1 x3@2 x4@3 x5@4;
  [ix sx];
  ix;
  sx@0;
  [x1-x5@0];

OUTPUT:
  TECH1 STDYX CINTERVAL;
")
writeLines(mplusSyntaxG2S, "modelg2s.inp")

# G3S: random linear slope
mplusSyntaxG3S <- ("
TITLE: G3S Random linear slope growth model - Stress;

DATA:
  FILE = modela.dat;

VARIABLE:
  NAMES = m2-m5 x1-x5 y1-y5 msbase0 Age0 gender race;
  USEVARIABLES = x1-x5;
  MISSING = ALL(-99);

ANALYSIS:
  ESTIMATOR = MLR;
  PROCESSORS = 6;

MODEL:
  ! Linear growth with random slope (individual differences in trajectory)
  ix sx | x1@0 x2@1 x3@2 x4@3 x5@4;
  [ix sx];
  ix;
  sx;
  ix WITH sx;
  [x1-x5@0];

OUTPUT:
  TECH1 STDYX CINTERVAL;
")
writeLines(mplusSyntaxG3S, "modelg3s.inp")

# G4S: freed time scores
mplusSyntaxG4S <- ("
TITLE: G4S Freed time scores growth model - Stress;
DATA:
  FILE = modela.dat;
VARIABLE:
  NAMES = m2-m5 x1-x5 y1-y5 msbase0 Age0 gender race;
  USEVARIABLES = x1-x5;
  MISSING = ALL(-99);
ANALYSIS:
  ESTIMATOR = MLR;
  PROCESSORS = 6;
  
MODEL:
  ! Freed time scores - intermediate loadings estimated freely
  ! x1 fixed at 0, x5 fixed at 1 for identification
  ix sx | x1@0 x2* x3* x4* x5@1;
  [ix sx];
  ix sx;
  ix WITH sx;
  [x1-x5@0];
OUTPUT:
  TECH1 STDYX CINTERVAL;
")
writeLines(mplusSyntaxG4S, "modelg4s.inp")
```

## Autoregressive Paths

Structured residuals capture each person's monthly deviation from their own trajectory. Autoregressive paths test whether a deviation carries over to the next month, first estimated freely and then constrained to be equal across months.

```{r autoregressive models}
# Stress: autoregressive paths free
mplusSyntaxG5S_free <- ("
TITLE: G5S_free Stress - freed time scores + free AR structured residuals;

DATA:
  FILE = modela.dat;

VARIABLE:
  NAMES = m2-m5 x1-x5 y1-y5 msbase0 Age0 gender race;
  USEVARIABLES = x1-x5;
  MISSING = ALL(-99);

ANALYSIS:
  ESTIMATOR = MLR;
  PROCESSORS = 6;

MODEL:
  ! Between-person growth factors with fixed freed time score loadings
  ix sx | x1@0 x2@0.126 x3@-0.194 x4@-0.695 x5@1;
  [ix sx];
  ix sx;
  ix WITH sx;
  [x1-x5@0];

  ! Structured residuals - transfer all residual variance to latent factors
  rx1 BY x1@1;
  rx2 BY x2@1;
  rx3 BY x3@1;
  rx4 BY x4@1;
  rx5 BY x5@1;
  [rx1-rx5@0];
  x1-x5@0;

  ! Wave 1 SR variance freely estimated (unconditioned)
  ! Waves 2-5 SR variances constrained to equality (conditioned on prior residual)
  rx1;
  rx2-rx5 (vsx);

  ! Freely estimated autoregressive paths
  rx2 ON rx1 (ar1x);
  rx3 ON rx2 (ar2x);
  rx4 ON rx3 (ar3x);
  rx5 ON rx4 (ar4x);

OUTPUT:
  TECH1 STDYX CINTERVAL;
")
writeLines(mplusSyntaxG5S_free, "modelg5s_free.inp")

# Stress: autoregressive paths equal
mplusSyntaxG5S_eq <- ("
TITLE: G5S_eq Stress - freed time scores + equality-constrained AR structured residuals;

DATA:
  FILE = modela.dat;

VARIABLE:
  NAMES = m2-m5 x1-x5 y1-y5 msbase0 Age0 gender race;
  USEVARIABLES = x1-x5;
  MISSING = ALL(-99);

ANALYSIS:
  ESTIMATOR = MLR;
  PROCESSORS = 6;

MODEL:
  ! Between-person growth factors with fixed freed time score loadings
  ix sx | x1@0 x2@0.126 x3@-0.194 x4@-0.695 x5@1;
  [ix sx];
  ix sx;
  ix WITH sx;
  [x1-x5@0];

  ! Structured residuals
  rx1 BY x1@1;
  rx2 BY x2@1;
  rx3 BY x3@1;
  rx4 BY x4@1;
  rx5 BY x5@1;
  [rx1-rx5@0];
  x1-x5@0;

  rx1;
  rx2-rx5 (vsx);

  ! Equality-constrained autoregressive paths
  rx2 ON rx1 (arx);
  rx3 ON rx2 (arx);
  rx4 ON rx3 (arx);
  rx5 ON rx4 (arx);

OUTPUT:
  TECH1 STDYX CINTERVAL;
")
writeLines(mplusSyntaxG5S_eq, "modelg5s_eq.inp")

# Distress: autoregressive paths free
mplusSyntaxG5D_free <- ("
TITLE: G5D_free Distress - random linear slope + free AR structured residuals;

DATA:
  FILE = modela.dat;

VARIABLE:
  NAMES = m2-m5 x1-x5 y1-y5 msbase0 Age0 gender race;
  USEVARIABLES = y1-y5;
  MISSING = ALL(-99);

ANALYSIS:
  ESTIMATOR = MLR;
  PROCESSORS = 6;

MODEL:
  ! Between-person growth factors - linear loadings retained from G3D
  iy sy | y1@0 y2@1 y3@2 y4@3 y5@4;
  [iy sy];
  iy;
  sy;
  iy WITH sy;
  [y1-y5@0];

  ! Structured residuals
  ry1 BY y1@1;
  ry2 BY y2@1;
  ry3 BY y3@1;
  ry4 BY y4@1;
  ry5 BY y5@1;
  [ry1-ry5@0];
  y1-y5@0;

  ! Wave 1 SR variance freely estimated (unconditioned)
  ! Waves 2-5 SR variances constrained to equality
  ry1;
  ry2-ry5 (vdy);

  ! Freely estimated autoregressive paths
  ry2 ON ry1 (ar1y);
  ry3 ON ry2 (ar2y);
  ry4 ON ry3 (ar3y);
  ry5 ON ry4 (ar4y);

OUTPUT:
  TECH1 STDYX CINTERVAL;
")
writeLines(mplusSyntaxG5D_free, "modelg5d_free.inp")

# Distress: autoregressive paths equal
mplusSyntaxG5D_eq <- ("
TITLE: G5D_eq Distress - random linear slope + equality-constrained AR structured residuals;

DATA:
  FILE = modela.dat;

VARIABLE:
  NAMES = m2-m5 x1-x5 y1-y5 msbase0 Age0 gender race;
  USEVARIABLES = y1-y5;
  MISSING = ALL(-99);

ANALYSIS:
  ESTIMATOR = MLR;
  PROCESSORS = 6;

MODEL:
  iy sy | y1@0 y2@1 y3@2 y4@3 y5@4;
  [iy sy];
  iy;
  sy;
  iy WITH sy;
  [y1-y5@0];

  ry1 BY y1@1;
  ry2 BY y2@1;
  ry3 BY y3@1;
  ry4 BY y4@1;
  ry5 BY y5@1;
  [ry1-ry5@0];
  y1-y5@0;

  ry1;
  ry2-ry5 (vdy);

  ! Equality-constrained autoregressive paths
  ry2 ON ry1 (ary);
  ry3 ON ry2 (ary);
  ry4 ON ry3 (ary);
  ry5 ON ry4 (ary);

OUTPUT:
  TECH1 STDYX CINTERVAL;
")
writeLines(mplusSyntaxG5D_eq, "modelg5d_eq.inp")
```

```{r run autoregressive models}
runModels("modelg5s_free.inp")
runModels("modelg5s_eq.inp")
runModels("modelg5d_free.inp")
runModels("modelg5d_eq.inp")

rbind(
  "Distress: adding autoregressive paths"        = scaled_diff_test("modelg3d.out", "modelg5d_free.out"),
  "Stress: equal vs free autoregressive paths"   = scaled_diff_test("modelg5s_eq.out", "modelg5s_free.out"), # this test is not interpretable because the free model was under-identified, as the Results explain.
  "Distress: equal vs free autoregressive paths" = scaled_diff_test("modelg5d_eq.out", "modelg5d_free.out")
)
```

# Part 4: Bivariate Model (Supplementary Material S3)

Stress and distress are combined in one model. Baseline distress group (`dgrp`) is added as a covariate from this point.

```{r mplus data b}
mplus_b <- GZMCore %>%
  select(m_W1, m_W2, m_W3, m_W4, x1, x2, x3, x4, x5, y1, y2, y3, y4, y5,
         msbase0, Age0, gender, race, dgrp)
mplus_b[is.na(mplus_b)] <- -99
prepareMplusData(mplus_b, "modelb.dat")
```

## Distress Slope

With a random distress slope, the bivariate model was inadmissible (a negative residual variance, or Heywood case). This model is kept to show the problem. The distress slope variance is fixed to zero in all later models.

```{r random distress slope}
# Random distress slope (inadmissible)
mplusSyntaxBiv1_randomslope <- ("
TITLE: BIV1_randomslope Bivariate LCM-SR - random distress slope (Heywood case);

DATA:
  FILE = modelb.dat;

VARIABLE:
  NAMES = m2-m5 x1-x5 y1-y5 msbase0 Age0 gender race dgrp;
  USEVARIABLES = x1-x5 y1-y5 dgrp;
  MISSING = ALL(-99);

ANALYSIS:
  ESTIMATOR = MLR;
  PROCESSORS = 6;

MODEL:
  ! Stress: freed time scores trajectory
  ix sx | x1@0 x2@0.126 x3@-0.194 x4@-0.695 x5@1;
  [ix sx];
  ix sx;
  ix WITH sx;

  ! Distress: random linear slope (as selected at univariate stage)
  iy sy | y1@0 y2@1 y3@2 y4@3 y5@4;
  [iy sy];
  iy sy;
  iy WITH sy;

  ! Between-person cross-construct covariances
  ix WITH iy; ix WITH sy;
  sx WITH iy; sx WITH sy;

  [x1-x5@0];
  [y1-y5@0];

  ! Stress structured residuals
  rx1 BY x1@1; rx2 BY x2@1; rx3 BY x3@1; rx4 BY x4@1; rx5 BY x5@1;
  [rx1-rx5@0];
  x1-x5@0;

  ! Distress structured residuals
  ry1 BY y1@1; ry2 BY y2@1; ry3 BY y3@1; ry4 BY y4@1; ry5 BY y5@1;
  [ry1-ry5@0];
  y1-y5@0;

  rx1;
  rx2-rx5 (vsx);
  ry1;
  ry2-ry5 (vdy);

  ! Stress AR - equality constrained
  rx2 ON rx1 (arx);
  rx3 ON rx2 (arx);
  rx4 ON rx3 (arx);
  rx5 ON rx4 (arx);

  ! Distress AR - equality constrained (as per univariate stage)
  ry2 ON ry1 (ary);
  ry3 ON ry2 (ary);
  ry4 ON ry3 (ary);
  ry5 ON ry4 (ary);

  ! Within-time covariances
  rx1 WITH ry1;
  rx2 WITH ry2 (wcov);
  rx3 WITH ry3 (wcov);
  rx4 WITH ry4 (wcov);
  rx5 WITH ry5 (wcov);

  ix ON dgrp;
  sx ON dgrp;
  iy ON dgrp;
  sy ON dgrp;

OUTPUT:
  TECH1 STDYX CINTERVAL;
")
writeLines(mplusSyntaxBiv1_randomslope, "modelbiv1_randomslope.inp")
runModels("modelbiv1_randomslope.inp")

# Warning lines in the output
grep("NEGATIVE|NOT POSITIVE DEFINITE", readLines("modelbiv1_randomslope.out"), value = TRUE)
```

## Within-Time Covariances

Same-month stress and distress deviations are allowed to covary. This tests whether that covariance can be held equal across months.

```{r within-time covariances}
# Covariances equal across W1-W4
mplusSyntaxBiv1 <- ("
TITLE: BIV1 Bivariate LCM-SR - growth factors covarying, no cross-lags;

DATA:
  FILE = modelb.dat;

VARIABLE:
  NAMES = m2-m5 x1-x5 y1-y5 msbase0 Age0 gender race dgrp;
  USEVARIABLES = x1-x5 y1-y5 dgrp;
  MISSING = ALL(-99);

ANALYSIS:
  ESTIMATOR = MLR;
  PROCESSORS = 6;

MODEL:
  !-----------------------------------------------------------------
  ! BETWEEN-PERSON COMPONENT
  !-----------------------------------------------------------------

  ! Stress: freed time scores trajectory (loadings fixed from G4S)
  ix sx | x1@0 x2@0.126 x3@-0.194 x4@-0.695 x5@1;
  [ix sx];
  ix sx;
  ix WITH sx;

  ! Distress: fixed linear slope (slope variance fixed to zero)
  ! Random slope caused Heywood case in bivariate context
  iy sy | y1@0 y2@1 y3@2 y4@3 y5@4;
  [iy sy];
  iy;
  sy@0;

  ! Between-person covariances across constructs
  ! sy omitted as its variance is fixed to zero
  ix WITH iy;
  sx WITH iy;

  !-----------------------------------------------------------------
  ! WITHIN-PERSON COMPONENT - STRUCTURED RESIDUALS
  !-----------------------------------------------------------------

  [x1-x5@0];
  [y1-y5@0];

  ! Stress structured residuals
  rx1 BY x1@1; rx2 BY x2@1; rx3 BY x3@1; rx4 BY x4@1; rx5 BY x5@1;
  [rx1-rx5@0];
  x1-x5@0;

  ! Distress structured residuals
  ry1 BY y1@1; ry2 BY y2@1; ry3 BY y3@1; ry4 BY y4@1; ry5 BY y5@1;
  [ry1-ry5@0];
  y1-y5@0;

  ! Stress SR variances: W1 free, W2-5 equality constrained
  rx1;
  rx2-rx5 (vsx);

  ! Distress SR variances: W1 free, W2-5 equality constrained
  ry1;
  ry2-ry5 (vdy);

  ! Stress AR paths - equality constrained (stationary)
  rx2 ON rx1 (arx);
  rx3 ON rx2 (arx);
  rx4 ON rx3 (arx);
  rx5 ON rx4 (arx);

  ! Distress AR paths - freely estimated (non-stationary)
  ry2 ON ry1;
  ry3 ON ry2;
  ry4 ON ry3;
  ry5 ON ry4;

  ! Within-time residual covariances
  ! W1 freely estimated, W2-5 constrained to equality
  rx1 WITH ry1;
  rx2 WITH ry2 (wcov);
  rx3 WITH ry3 (wcov);
  rx4 WITH ry4 (wcov);
  rx5 WITH ry5 (wcov);

  ! Covariate: dgrp predicts stress and distress growth factors
  ! sy omitted as its variance is fixed
  ix ON dgrp;
  sx ON dgrp;
  iy ON dgrp;

OUTPUT:
  TECH1 STDYX CINTERVAL;
")
writeLines(mplusSyntaxBiv1, "modelbiv1.inp")

# Covariances free at each wave (retained)
mplusSyntaxBiv1_free <- ("
TITLE: BIV1_free Bivariate LCM-SR - within-time covariances freely estimated;

DATA:
  FILE = modelb.dat;

VARIABLE:
  NAMES = m2-m5 x1-x5 y1-y5 msbase0 Age0 gender race dgrp;
  USEVARIABLES = x1-x5 y1-y5 dgrp;
  MISSING = ALL(-99);

ANALYSIS:
  ESTIMATOR = MLR;
  PROCESSORS = 6;

MODEL:
  ix sx | x1@0 x2@0.126 x3@-0.194 x4@-0.695 x5@1;
  [ix sx];
  ix sx;
  ix WITH sx;

  iy sy | y1@0 y2@1 y3@2 y4@3 y5@4;
  [iy sy];
  iy;
  sy@0;

  ix WITH iy;
  sx WITH iy;

  [x1-x5@0];
  [y1-y5@0];

  rx1 BY x1@1; rx2 BY x2@1; rx3 BY x3@1; rx4 BY x4@1; rx5 BY x5@1;
  [rx1-rx5@0];
  x1-x5@0;

  ry1 BY y1@1; ry2 BY y2@1; ry3 BY y3@1; ry4 BY y4@1; ry5 BY y5@1;
  [ry1-ry5@0];
  y1-y5@0;

  rx1;
  rx2-rx5 (vsx);
  ry1;
  ry2-ry5 (vdy);

  rx2 ON rx1 (arx);
  rx3 ON rx2 (arx);
  rx4 ON rx3 (arx);
  rx5 ON rx4 (arx);

  ry2 ON ry1;
  ry3 ON ry2;
  ry4 ON ry3;
  ry5 ON ry4;

  ! Within-time covariances freely estimated across all waves
  rx1 WITH ry1;
  rx2 WITH ry2;
  rx3 WITH ry3;
  rx4 WITH ry4;
  rx5 WITH ry5;

  ix ON dgrp;
  sx ON dgrp;
  iy ON dgrp;

OUTPUT:
  TECH1 STDYX CINTERVAL;
")
writeLines(mplusSyntaxBiv1_free, "modelbiv1_free.inp")

runModels("modelbiv1.inp")
runModels("modelbiv1_free.inp")

scaled_diff_test("modelbiv1.out", "modelbiv1_free.out")
```

## Cross-Lagged Paths

Does a stress deviation predict next month's distress deviation, or the reverse? Neither direction improved fit, so cross-lagged paths were not retained (Figure 1).

```{r cross-lagged models}
# Stress to next-month distress
mplusSyntaxBiv2a <- ("
TITLE: BIV2a Bivariate LCM-SR - cross-lag stress to distress only;

DATA:
  FILE = modelb.dat;

VARIABLE:
  NAMES = m2-m5 x1-x5 y1-y5 msbase0 Age0 gender race dgrp;
  USEVARIABLES = x1-x5 y1-y5 dgrp;
  MISSING = ALL(-99);

ANALYSIS:
  ESTIMATOR = MLR;
  PROCESSORS = 6;

MODEL:
  ! Stress trajectory - freed time scores
  ix sx | x1@0 x2@0.126 x3@-0.194 x4@-0.695 x5@1;
  [ix sx];
  ix sx;
  ix WITH sx;

  ! Distress trajectory - fixed slope
  iy sy | y1@0 y2@1 y3@2 y4@3 y5@4;
  [iy sy];
  iy;
  sy@0;

  ! Between-person cross-construct covariances
  ! sy omitted as variance is fixed to zero
  ix WITH iy;
  sx WITH iy;

  [x1-x5@0];
  [y1-y5@0];

  ! Stress structured residuals
  rx1 BY x1@1; rx2 BY x2@1; rx3 BY x3@1; rx4 BY x4@1; rx5 BY x5@1;
  [rx1-rx5@0];
  x1-x5@0;

  ! Distress structured residuals
  ry1 BY y1@1; ry2 BY y2@1; ry3 BY y3@1; ry4 BY y4@1; ry5 BY y5@1;
  [ry1-ry5@0];
  y1-y5@0;

  ! SR variances
  rx1;
  rx2-rx5 (vsx);
  ry1;
  ry2-ry5 (vdy);

  ! Stress AR - equality constrained (stationary)
  rx2 ON rx1 (arx);
  rx3 ON rx2 (arx);
  rx4 ON rx3 (arx);
  rx5 ON rx4 (arx);

  ! Distress AR - freely estimated (non-stationary)
  ry2 ON ry1;
  ry3 ON ry2;
  ry4 ON ry3;
  ry5 ON ry4;

  ! Within-time covariances
  rx1 WITH ry1;
  rx2 WITH ry2;
  rx3 WITH ry3;
  rx4 WITH ry4;
  rx5 WITH ry5;

  ! Cross-lagged paths: stress predicting subsequent distress only
  ! Equality constrained across lags
  ry2 ON rx1 (cl_xy);
  ry3 ON rx2 (cl_xy);
  ry4 ON rx3 (cl_xy);
  ry5 ON rx4 (cl_xy);

  ! Covariates
  ix ON dgrp;
  sx ON dgrp;
  iy ON dgrp;

OUTPUT:
  TECH1 STDYX CINTERVAL;
")
```

```{r run cross-lagged models}

  "Both directions vs none"              = scaled_diff_test("modelbiv1_free.out", "modelbiv2c.out"),
  "Adding distress to stress"            = scaled_diff_test("modelbiv2a.out", "modelbiv2c.out"),
  "Adding stress to distress"            = scaled_diff_test("modelbiv2b.out", "modelbiv2c.out")
)
```

# Part 5: Identity Development Experience Effects (Table S2)

Monthly identity development experience counts predict the same-month stress and distress deviations (contemporaneous), next month's deviations (lagged), or both. The contemporaneous model was retained.

```{r identity experience models}
# No identity experience paths
mplusSyntaxBiv1_sides <- ("
TITLE: BIV1_sides Bivariate baseline with SIDEs included but no paths to residuals;

DATA:
  FILE = modelb.dat;

VARIABLE:
  NAMES = m2-m5 x1-x5 y1-y5 msbase0 Age0 gender race dgrp;
  USEVARIABLES = m2-m5 x1-x5 y1-y5 dgrp;
  MISSING = ALL(-99);

ANALYSIS:
  ESTIMATOR = MLR;
  PROCESSORS = 6;

MODEL:
  ! Stress trajectory
  ix sx | x1@0 x2@0.126 x3@-0.194 x4@-0.695 x5@1;
  [ix sx];
  ix sx;
  ix WITH sx;

  ! Distress trajectory
  iy sy | y1@0 y2@1 y3@2 y4@3 y5@4;
  [iy sy];
  iy;
  sy@0;

  ! Between-person cross-construct covariances
  ix WITH iy;
  sx WITH iy;

  [x1-x5@0];
  [y1-y5@0];

  ! Stress structured residuals
  rx1 BY x1@1; rx2 BY x2@1; rx3 BY x3@1; rx4 BY x4@1; rx5 BY x5@1;
  [rx1-rx5@0];
  x1-x5@0;

  ! Distress structured residuals
  ry1 BY y1@1; ry2 BY y2@1; ry3 BY y3@1; ry4 BY y4@1; ry5 BY y5@1;
  [ry1-ry5@0];
  y1-y5@0;

  rx1;
  rx2-rx5 (vsx);
  ry1;
  ry2-ry5 (vdy);

  ! Within-construct AR paths
  rx2 ON rx1 (arx);
  rx3 ON rx2 (arx);
  rx4 ON rx3 (arx);
  rx5 ON rx4 (arx);

  ry2 ON ry1;
  ry3 ON ry2;
  ry4 ON ry3;
  ry5 ON ry4;

  ! Within-time covariances
  rx1 WITH ry1;
  rx2 WITH ry2;
  rx3 WITH ry3;
  rx4 WITH ry4;
  rx5 WITH ry5;

  ! SIDEs included as endogenous but no paths to residuals
  ! This makes the variable set and N identical to BIV3 models
  [m2-m5];
  m2-m5;

  ! Distress group covariate
  ix ON dgrp;
  sx ON dgrp;
  iy ON dgrp;

OUTPUT:
  TECH1 STDYX CINTERVAL;
")
writeLines(mplusSyntaxBiv1_sides, "modelbiv1_sides.inp")

# Contemporaneous effects (retained)
mplusSyntaxBiv3a <- ("
TITLE: BIV3a Bivariate LCM-SR - SIDEs contemporaneous only;

DATA:
  FILE = modelb.dat;

VARIABLE:
  NAMES = m2-m5 x1-x5 y1-y5 msbase0 Age0 gender race dgrp;
  USEVARIABLES = m2-m5 x1-x5 y1-y5 dgrp;
  MISSING = ALL(-99);

ANALYSIS:
  ESTIMATOR = MLR;
  PROCESSORS = 6;

MODEL:
  ! Stress trajectory
  ix sx | x1@0 x2@0.126 x3@-0.194 x4@-0.695 x5@1;
  [ix sx];
  ix sx;
  ix WITH sx;

  ! Distress trajectory
  iy sy | y1@0 y2@1 y3@2 y4@3 y5@4;
  [iy sy];
  iy;
  sy@0;

  ! Between-person cross-construct covariances
  ix WITH iy;
  sx WITH iy;

  [x1-x5@0];
  [y1-y5@0];

  ! Stress structured residuals
  rx1 BY x1@1; rx2 BY x2@1; rx3 BY x3@1; rx4 BY x4@1; rx5 BY x5@1;
  [rx1-rx5@0];
  x1-x5@0;

  ! Distress structured residuals
  ry1 BY y1@1; ry2 BY y2@1; ry3 BY y3@1; ry4 BY y4@1; ry5 BY y5@1;
  [ry1-ry5@0];
  y1-y5@0;

  rx1;
  rx2-rx5 (vsx);
  ry1;
  ry2-ry5 (vdy);

  ! Within-construct AR paths
  rx2 ON rx1 (arx);
  rx3 ON rx2 (arx);
  rx4 ON rx3 (arx);
  rx5 ON rx4 (arx);

  ry2 ON ry1;
  ry3 ON ry2;
  ry4 ON ry3;
  ry5 ON ry4;

  ! Within-time covariances
  rx1 WITH ry1;
  rx2 WITH ry2;
  rx3 WITH ry3;
  rx4 WITH ry4;
  rx5 WITH ry5;

  ! Contemporaneous SIDE effects on stress residuals
  ! m2 = SIDEs at W1-W2 interval, predicts rx2 (W2 deviation), etc.
  ! Constrained to equality across waves
  rx2 ON m2 (sides_x_con);
  rx3 ON m3 (sides_x_con);
  rx4 ON m4 (sides_x_con);
  rx5 ON m5 (sides_x_con);

  ! Contemporaneous SIDE effects on distress residuals
  ry2 ON m2 (sides_y_con);
  ry3 ON m3 (sides_y_con);
  ry4 ON m4 (sides_y_con);
  ry5 ON m5 (sides_y_con);

  ! Distress group covariate
  ix ON dgrp;
  sx ON dgrp;
  iy ON dgrp;
  
  [m2-m5];
  m2-m5;

OUTPUT:
  TECH1 STDYX CINTERVAL;
")
writeLines(mplusSyntaxBiv3a, "modelbiv3a.inp")

# Lagged effects
mplusSyntaxBiv3b <- ("
TITLE: BIV3b Bivariate LCM-SR - SIDEs lagged only;

DATA:
  FILE = modelb.dat;

VARIABLE:
  NAMES = m2-m5 x1-x5 y1-y5 msbase0 Age0 gender race dgrp;
  USEVARIABLES = m2-m5 x1-x5 y1-y5 dgrp;
  MISSING = ALL(-99);

ANALYSIS:
  ESTIMATOR = MLR;
  PROCESSORS = 6;

MODEL:
  ! Stress trajectory
  ix sx | x1@0 x2@0.126 x3@-0.194 x4@-0.695 x5@1;
  [ix sx];
  ix sx;
  ix WITH sx;

  ! Distress trajectory
  iy sy | y1@0 y2@1 y3@2 y4@3 y5@4;
  [iy sy];
  iy;
  sy@0;

  ! Between-person cross-construct covariances
  ix WITH iy;
  sx WITH iy;

  [x1-x5@0];
  [y1-y5@0];

  ! Stress structured residuals
  rx1 BY x1@1; rx2 BY x2@1; rx3 BY x3@1; rx4 BY x4@1; rx5 BY x5@1;
  [rx1-rx5@0];
  x1-x5@0;

  ! Distress structured residuals
  ry1 BY y1@1; ry2 BY y2@1; ry3 BY y3@1; ry4 BY y4@1; ry5 BY y5@1;
  [ry1-ry5@0];
  y1-y5@0;

  rx1;
  rx2-rx5 (vsx);
  ry1;
  ry2-ry5 (vdy);

  ! Within-construct AR paths
  rx2 ON rx1 (arx);
  rx3 ON rx2 (arx);
  rx4 ON rx3 (arx);
  rx5 ON rx4 (arx);

  ry2 ON ry1;
  ry3 ON ry2;
  ry4 ON ry3;
  ry5 ON ry4;

  ! Within-time covariances
  rx1 WITH ry1;
  rx2 WITH ry2;
  rx3 WITH ry3;
  rx4 WITH ry4;
  rx5 WITH ry5;
  
  ! Lagged SIDE effects on stress residuals
  ! m2 = SIDEs at W1-W2 interval predicts rx3 (next wave deviation), etc.
  ! Constrained to equality across waves
  rx3 ON m2 (sides_x_lag);
  rx4 ON m3 (sides_x_lag);
  rx5 ON m4 (sides_x_lag);

  ! Lagged SIDE effects on distress residuals
  ry3 ON m2 (sides_y_lag);
  ry4 ON m3 (sides_y_lag);
  ry5 ON m4 (sides_y_lag);

  ! Distress group covariate
  ix ON dgrp;
  sx ON dgrp;
  iy ON dgrp;
  
  [m2-m5];
  m2-m5;

OUTPUT:
  TECH1 STDYX CINTERVAL;
")
writeLines(mplusSyntaxBiv3b, "modelbiv3b.inp")

# Contemporaneous and lagged effects
mplusSyntaxBiv3c <- ("
TITLE: BIV3c Bivariate LCM-SR - SIDEs contemporaneous and lagged;

DATA:
  FILE = modelb.dat;

VARIABLE:
  NAMES = m2-m5 x1-x5 y1-y5 msbase0 Age0 gender race dgrp;
  USEVARIABLES = m2-m5 x1-x5 y1-y5 dgrp;
  MISSING = ALL(-99);

ANALYSIS:
  ESTIMATOR = MLR;
  PROCESSORS = 6;

MODEL:
  ! Stress trajectory
  ix sx | x1@0 x2@0.126 x3@-0.194 x4@-0.695 x5@1;
  [ix sx];
  ix sx;
  ix WITH sx;

  ! Distress trajectory
  iy sy | y1@0 y2@1 y3@2 y4@3 y5@4;
  [iy sy];
  iy;
  sy@0;

  ! Between-person cross-construct covariances
  ix WITH iy;
  sx WITH iy;

  [x1-x5@0];
  [y1-y5@0];

  ! Stress structured residuals
  rx1 BY x1@1; rx2 BY x2@1; rx3 BY x3@1; rx4 BY x4@1; rx5 BY x5@1;
  [rx1-rx5@0];
  x1-x5@0;

  ! Distress structured residuals
  ry1 BY y1@1; ry2 BY y2@1; ry3 BY y3@1; ry4 BY y4@1; ry5 BY y5@1;
  [ry1-ry5@0];
  y1-y5@0;

  rx1;
  rx2-rx5 (vsx);
  ry1;
  ry2-ry5 (vdy);

  ! Within-construct AR paths
  rx2 ON rx1 (arx);
  rx3 ON rx2 (arx);
  rx4 ON rx3 (arx);
  rx5 ON rx4 (arx);

  ry2 ON ry1;
  ry3 ON ry2;
  ry4 ON ry3;
  ry5 ON ry4;

  ! Within-time covariances
  rx1 WITH ry1;
  rx2 WITH ry2;
  rx3 WITH ry3;
  rx4 WITH ry4;
  rx5 WITH ry5;

  ! Contemporaneous SIDE effects
  rx2 ON m2 (sides_x_con);
  rx3 ON m3 (sides_x_con);
  rx4 ON m4 (sides_x_con);
  rx5 ON m5 (sides_x_con);

  ry2 ON m2 (sides_y_con);
  ry3 ON m3 (sides_y_con);
  ry4 ON m4 (sides_y_con);
  ry5 ON m5 (sides_y_con);

  ! Lagged SIDE effects
  rx3 ON m2 (sides_x_lag);
  rx4 ON m3 (sides_x_lag);
  rx5 ON m4 (sides_x_lag);

  ry3 ON m2 (sides_y_lag);
  ry4 ON m3 (sides_y_lag);
  ry5 ON m4 (sides_y_lag);

  ! Distress group covariate
  ix ON dgrp;
  sx ON dgrp;
  iy ON dgrp;
  
  [m2-m5];
  m2-m5;

OUTPUT:
  TECH1 STDYX CINTERVAL;
")
writeLines(mplusSyntaxBiv3c, "modelbiv3c.inp")
```

```{r run identity experience models}
runModels("modelbiv1_sides.inp")
runModels("modelbiv3a.inp")
runModels("modelbiv3b.inp")
runModels("modelbiv3c.inp")
```

```{r table s2}
table_s2 <- bind_rows(
  readModels("modelbiv1_sides.out", what = "summaries")$summaries,
  readModels("modelbiv3a.out",      what = "summaries")$summaries,
  readModels("modelbiv3b.out",      what = "summaries")$summaries,

) %>%
  select(any_of(fit_cols))

table_s2
write.csv(table_s2, "TableS2_identity_experience_fit.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Does adding lagged paths to the contemporaneous model improve fit?
scaled_diff_test("modelbiv3a.out", "modelbiv3c.out")
```

```{r identity experience paths}
# Standardised identity experience paths in each model (reported in S3)
# m2 to m5 = identity experience counts at W1 to W4
biv3a <- readModels("modelbiv3a.out", what = "parameters")$parameters$stdyx.standardized
biv3b <- readModels("modelbiv3b.out", what = "parameters")$parameters$stdyx.standardized
biv3c <- readModels("modelbiv3c.out", what = "parameters")$parameters$stdyx.standardized

filter(biv3a, param %in% c("M2", "M3", "M4", "M5"))
filter(biv3b, param %in% c("M2", "M3", "M4", "M5"))
filter(biv3c, param %in% c("M2", "M3", "M4", "M5"))
```

# Part 6: Final Model (Table 4 and Figure 1)

Covariates are added to the retained model: baseline distress group, age, gender, ethnoracial identity and baseline (lifetime) identity experience count. They predict the growth factors and the monthly identity experience counts.

```{r final model}
mplusSyntaxBiv3a_cond <- ("
TITLE: BIV3a_cond Final conditional LCM-SR - SIDEs contemporaneous + all covariates;

DATA:
  FILE = modelb.dat;

VARIABLE:
  NAMES = m2-m5 x1-x5 y1-y5 msbase0 Age0 gender race dgrp;
  USEVARIABLES = m2-m5 x1-x5 y1-y5 msbase0 Age0 gender race dgrp;
  MISSING = ALL(-99);

ANALYSIS:
  ESTIMATOR = MLR;
  PROCESSORS = 6;

MODEL:
  ! Stress trajectory - freed time scores
  ix sx | x1@0 x2@0.126 x3@-0.194 x4@-0.695 x5@1;
  [ix sx];
  ix sx;
  ix WITH sx;

  ! Distress trajectory - fixed slope
  iy sy | y1@0 y2@1 y3@2 y4@3 y5@4;
  [iy sy];
  iy;
  sy@0;

  ! Between-person cross-construct covariances
  ix WITH iy;
  sx WITH iy;

  [x1-x5@0];
  [y1-y5@0];

  ! Stress structured residuals
  rx1 BY x1@1; rx2 BY x2@1; rx3 BY x3@1; rx4 BY x4@1; rx5 BY x5@1;
  [rx1-rx5@0];
  x1-x5@0;

  ! Distress structured residuals
  ry1 BY y1@1; ry2 BY y2@1; ry3 BY y3@1; ry4 BY y4@1; ry5 BY y5@1;
  [ry1-ry5@0];
  y1-y5@0;

  rx1;
  rx2-rx5 (vsx);
  ry1;
  ry2-ry5 (vdy);

  ! Stress AR - equality constrained
  rx2 ON rx1 (arx);
  rx3 ON rx2 (arx);
  rx4 ON rx3 (arx);
  rx5 ON rx4 (arx);

  ! Distress AR - freely estimated
  ry2 ON ry1;
  ry3 ON ry2;
  ry4 ON ry3;
  ry5 ON ry4;

  ! Within-time covariances - freely estimated
  rx1 WITH ry1;
  rx2 WITH ry2;
  rx3 WITH ry3;
  rx4 WITH ry4;
  rx5 WITH ry5;

  ! Contemporaneous SIDE effects - equality constrained across waves
  rx2 ON m2 (sides_x_con);
  rx3 ON m3 (sides_x_con);
  rx4 ON m4 (sides_x_con);
  rx5 ON m5 (sides_x_con);

  ry2 ON m2 (sides_y_con);
  ry3 ON m3 (sides_y_con);
  ry4 ON m4 (sides_y_con);
  ry5 ON m5 (sides_y_con);

  ! Time-invariant covariates predicting growth factors
  ix ON dgrp Age0 gender race msbase0;
  sx ON dgrp Age0 gender race msbase0;
  iy ON dgrp Age0 gender race msbase0;
  
  ! Time-invariant covariates also predicting milestone exposure
  m2-m5 ON dgrp Age0 gender race msbase0;

OUTPUT:
  TECH1 STDYX CINTERVAL;
")
writeLines(mplusSyntaxBiv3a_cond, "modelbiv3a_cond.inp")
runModels("modelbiv3a_cond.inp")
```

```{r final model results}
final <- readModels("modelbiv3a_cond.out", what = c("summaries", "parameters"))

# Model fit
select(final$summaries, any_of(fit_cols))

# Standardised estimates (STDYX) with 95% confidence intervals, saved for Table 4
table_4 <- final$parameters$stdyx.standardized %>%
  left_join(select(final$parameters$ci.stdyx.standardized, paramHeader, param, low2.5, up2.5),
            by = c("paramHeader", "param"))
write.csv(table_4, "Table4_final_model.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Key results: identity experience effects on same-month stress (RX) and distress (RY)
filter(table_4, param %in% c("M2", "M3", "M4", "M5"))

# Key results: between-person covariances among the growth factors
filter(table_4, paramHeader %in% c("IX.WITH", "SX.WITH"))
```
